quote: Let X ~ MEG(eta, beta_1) and Y ~ MEG(eta, beta_2). If beta_2 > beta_1, then 1. X_{r:n} <=ST Y_{r:n} for r = 1, ..., n. 2. E(X_{r:n}) <= E(Y_{r:n}), provided the expectations exist.
family: MEG(eta, beta); iid samples from each distribution
compared: rth order statistics of iid samples from the two MEG laws
ambiguity: Via st-ordering preservation of order statistics (ref. [22], Theorem 4.4.1).

quote: Let X ~ MEG(eta, beta_1) and Y ~ MEG(eta, beta_2). If beta_2 > beta_1, then X <=LR Y.
model: other: two distributions of the same family
family: modified exponentiated family MEG(eta,beta): cdf F(y; eta, beta) = ([1+G(y;eta)]^beta - 1)/(2^beta - 1), pdf f = beta g (1+G)^{beta-1}/(2^beta - 1)
compared: shape parameter beta_1 vs beta_2, same parent G(eta)

quote: Let X1 and X2 be two Poisson-MEG mixtures with cdfs H1(x; beta_1) and H2(x; beta_2), respectively. If beta_2 > beta_1, then X1 <=LR X2.
family: Poisson-MEG mixture: X|Lambda=lambda ~ Poisson(lambda), Lambda ~ MEG(eta, beta)
ambiguity: Via Lambda_1 <=LR Lambda_2 (Prop. 3), Poisson TP2 property, and mixture preservation (Shaked-Shanthikumar Thm 1.C.17).
